pakistan-earthquake-roads-compensation-a.title: Land taken for earthquake road rebuilding, with a quarter of the compensation never reaching owners
pakistan-earthquake-roads-compensation-a.place: Jhelum Valley Road, Muzaffarabad, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and National Highways N-15 and N-35 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
pakistan-earthquake-roads-compensation-a.point: Muzaffarabad, the city the Jhelum Valley Road runs from, named in the completion report as one of the three roads rebuilt under this loan. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search for Muzaffarabad.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: First Additional Financing to the Highways Rehabilitation Project, project number P099040, a US$100.0 million loan (Ln. 7341-PK) approved on 1 December 2005, seven weeks after the 8 October 2005 earthquake, to reconstruct about 44 km of National Highway N-15 (the Kaghan Valley Road), rehabilitate about 25 km of National Highway N-35 (the Karakoram Highway) and rehabilitate about 59 km of the Jhelum Valley Road in Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and to pay for relocation of utilities, resettlement and land acquisition (Implementation Completion and Results Report, report no. ICR2723, 21 November 2013, section 1.6.1 and section 1.7.1(a)). The loan was one of four financings of a single operation carried under the parent project number P010556, which closed on 30 June 2013. That completion report rates the project's social safeguards Moderately Satisfactory (section 2.4.2) and its overall outcome Satisfactory; the Bank's Independent Evaluation Group rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, because efficiency was modest given significant cost overruns (ICR Review, 11 June 2014). The completion report says the Bank financed the land acquisition itself (Annex 7, p. 49).

companies.name: National Highway Authority
companies.role: Implementing agency. A federal body under Pakistan's Ministry of Communications that owns and manages the national highway network; its Project Management Unit ran the works, and its Deputy Project Coordinators kept the complaints register. The completion report's borrower section says land acquisition was held up by delay in releasing funds by the Authority, even though the Bank was paying for the land (Annex 7, p. 49). No construction contractor is named in the documents.

companies.name: Land Revenue Departments of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Azad Jammu and Kashmir
companies.role: Provincial and state revenue offices that assessed and paid out the compensation. The unpaid balance sat in their escrow accounts at project close. The completion report also records non-posting of required staff and a lukewarm response by the provincial revenue departments, and the destruction of revenue records in the earthquake.

pakistan-earthquake-roads-compensation-a.community: Rebuilding the three earthquake-damaged highways to national standards needed land. The completion report records about 1,007 kanals acquired for the Earthquake Damaged Roads component, valued at about Rs 108 million (US$1.1 million). Of that, Rs 76.5 million (US$0.78 million), 72 per cent, was paid to project-affected people. The remaining Rs 31 million (US$0.32 million) was not paid. The report gives four reasons: some owners died in the earthquake; some left the disaster areas for other parts of the country and could not be traced; some claims are disputed in court; and some are shamlat cases, land with many joint owners whose individual entitlements come to less than US$100 and who are unwilling to open a bank account to receive them. The report says the court cases are unlikely to be resolved in the near future, and that the money is already deposited and held in escrow accounts with the Land Revenue Departments, so compensation will eventually be paid when the cases settle. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group adds that the project team put the disputed claims at US$0.11 million, 36 per cent of the unpaid balance. The completion report's borrower section records that the Azad Jammu and Kashmir government used land acquisition funds for other purposes rather than disbursing them to affected people, and that the delay in acquiring land ran far enough that the Bank considered suspending disbursement. At appraisal in 2003, before the earthquake component was added, the project expected to take 6 hectares of land and affect about 350 people. On the main N-5 corridor the works stayed inside the existing right of way apart from five acres at Mitiari bypass, bought by private negotiation at market rates.
pakistan-earthquake-roads-compensation-a.outcome: The project closed on 30 June 2013. About Rs 31 million of compensation was still unpaid, held in escrow by the revenue departments of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, with the court cases behind part of it expected to take years. No later document showing the money paid out was found.
pakistan-earthquake-roads-compensation-a.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 513 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The completion report gives no count of people relocated on the earthquake roads.

sources.title: Pakistan - Highways Rehabilitation Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR2723), covering Ln. 7341-PK, the first Additional Financing approved 1 December 2005 (P099040)
Pakistan - Highways Rehabilitation Project: Implementation Completion Report (ICR) Review, Independent Evaluation Group

pakistan-earthquake-roads-compensation-a.confidence_note: The figures come from the Bank's own completion report and from the Independent Evaluation Group's review of that report, so the lender is reporting on its own project. No independent audit or court record covering this acquisition was found. Pakistan's Auditor General published a special audit of land acquisition for national highway and motorway projects for audit year 2016-17, but it does not deal with the three earthquake-damaged roads. A February 2019 report of a Senate committee hearing concerns unpaid acquisition on the Naran-Kaghan-Babusar Top stretch of the same highway, N-15, over a different and larger area, 1,698 kanals, and cannot be matched to this acquisition.

narayanghat-mugling-road-structures.title: Homes and shops hit by road widening and landslides on the Narayanghat-Mugling road
narayanghat-mugling-road-structures.place: Narayanghat-Mugling road, Chitwan and Tanahun districts, Nepal
narayanghat-mugling-road-structures.point: Mugling, the northern end of the 33 km road section upgraded under the project. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search for Mugling, Nepal.

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Nepal-India Regional Trade and Transport Project, project number P144335, credit IDA-52730 and grant IDA-H8630, approved 28 June 2013, effective 10 September 2013, closed 30 November 2021. US$99.0 million committed, US$70.5 million disbursed (Implementation Completion and Results Report, 22 June 2022, Financing and Key Dates tables). Component 1 upgraded and expanded the 33 km Narayanghat-Mugling section of the Birgunj-Kathmandu corridor to Asian Highway standard and built four bridges. The completion report rates the outcome Satisfactory and Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory; the Independent Evaluation Group concurs on the outcome and rates Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory (ICR Review, 14 September 2022, section 11).

companies.name: Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, Government of Nepal
companies.role: One of two implementing agencies named in the completion report. Its Department of Roads ran the Narayanghat-Mugling works through a project office at Mugling headed by a first-class engineer. No construction contractor is named; the report says three large works contracts were executed for the road.

narayanghat-mugling-road-structures.community: Upgrading the 33 km road hit 131 private structures, both homes and shops, belonging to 103 households. The completion report attributes the impacts to the road upgrade works and to landslides, and says the resettlement action plan of 2013 was updated three times, in 2014, 2016 and 2017, to deal with landslide impacts during construction. The outcome is larger than the plan: the Independent Evaluation Group records that 80 structures and 74 households were estimated at appraisal. Twenty community structures, mostly public toilets and passenger sheds, were also hit, and all twenty were rebuilt. Cash compensation, a displacement allowance, a rental stipend and a business disturbance allowance were paid to the affected households in line with the plan, except for one absentee household. Affected people also received an economic rehabilitation grant and income restoration training. A vulnerable community development plan covered project impacts on 91 households, mostly Dalit people and other minority ethnic groups.
narayanghat-mugling-road-structures.outcome: The project closed on 30 November 2021 with most of the road improvements finished by mid-2018. Slope works at km 17 and km 26 were not completed within the project period because of the covid-19 pandemic. One affected household remained uncompensated because its owner was absent.
narayanghat-mugling-road-structures.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 414 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The completion report counts structures and households hit, not people relocated, although it records that a displacement allowance and a rental stipend were paid.
narayanghat-mugling-road-structures.displaced_label: No count of people relocated appears in the completion report; 131 private structures belonging to 103 households were impacted.

sources.title: Nepal - Nepal-India Regional Trade And Transport Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P144335)
Nepal - Nepal-India Regional Trade And Transport Project: Implementation Completion Report (ICR) Review, Independent Evaluation Group

narayanghat-mugling-road-structures.confidence_note: Both the structure count and the account of compensation come from the Bank's completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of it, so the lender is reporting on its own project. The two documents agree on the figures, and the review records the appraisal estimates the outcome exceeded, which rules out a plan figure reprinted as a result. No independent field study or press report on the Narayanghat-Mugling compensation was found. Neither document says how many of the 103 households had to move.

chobhar-dry-port-arrests-kathmandu.title: Arrests at the Chobhar dry port groundbreaking, and unsettled land claims under the site
chobhar-dry-port-arrests-kathmandu.point: Chobhar, the village in Kirtipur Municipality where the inland container depot was built. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search for Chobhar, Kathmandu.

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Nepal-India Regional Trade and Transport Project, project number P144335, credit IDA-52730 and grant IDA-H8630, approved 28 June 2013, effective 10 September 2013, closed 30 November 2021 (Implementation Completion and Results Report, 22 June 2022). The project financed the Kathmandu inland container depot at Chobhar. The Bank told the Inspection Panel on 15 May 2020 that disbursements for the dry port had been withheld until February 2020 to address grievances and were then authorised because the grievances had been resolved (Inspection Panel Notice of Registration, 27 May 2020, paragraph 18). The project was restructured in December 2019 to extend the closing date by 23 months.

companies.name: Nepal Intermodal Transport Development Board
companies.role: The state body that built the dry port, under Nepal's Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, which the completion report names as an implementing agency. It ran the grievance notices the requesters answered.

companies.name: Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Government of Nepal
companies.role: Implementing agency named in the completion report for the trade component, which included the Kathmandu depot.

chobhar-dry-port-arrests-kathmandu.community: The depot was built on land at Chobhar, in Kirtipur Municipality south of Kathmandu, that the state had acquired decades earlier for the Himal Cement Factory, closed in 2002. Residents, mainly indigenous Newars, said the land should go back to its original owners and that disputes over that old acquisition were never settled. The Kathmandu Post reported on 18 January 2019 that the government said it had acquired 1,054 ropanis from the former factory, 228 ropanis of it for the dry port and 826 for an international exhibition centre, and quoted Panchha Lal Maharjan of the Chobhar Conservation Committee saying the government had not acquired all the private land, had not paid 416 former cement factory workers for 19 months, and had not compensated people whose houses were destroyed when the factory was built. The Board's Rabi Shankar Sainju said an audit showed no employee liabilities but that the Board would raise it with the Finance Ministry if the claim was genuine. Local groups stopped the depot works from August 2018 to January 2019, and the Bank told the government it would make no disbursement against the component until community grievances were addressed and the grievance process documented. A two-tier grievance mechanism was then set up, with a committee at the site and one at the ministry.
chobhar-dry-port-arrests-kathmandu.suppression: Nepal's Prime Minister laid the foundation stone for the dry port on 17 January 2019. The Kathmandu Post reported the next day that around 150 locals had gathered from the morning and that police arrested at least 54 of them, on figures given by the Chobhar Conservation Committee's coordinator. The Request for Inspection later filed with the World Bank's Inspection Panel says fifty-two locals were detained from the streets and from their houses, that the event took place under an undeclared curfew in the construction area, and that construction has gone on behind Armed Police Force guards. The two accounts differ on the number detained, 52 against at least 54.
chobhar-dry-port-arrests-kathmandu.outcome: The Inspection Panel registered the request on 27 May 2020. After visiting the site and meeting the requesters, the Panel found no sufficient grounds to investigate the complaint, and recommended that consultations with local communities be strengthened in future projects. The Bank told the Panel that several of the complaints concerned actions long predating its involvement, such as land claims going back to the 1960s, and that these were outside the policy's scope. The Bank also said the project recognised the Newars as indigenous peoples and that the policy did not require a separate Indigenous Peoples Plan. Disbursements for the dry port resumed in February 2020. The project closed on 30 November 2021. The requesters say their demand for the return of the land has not been acted on.
chobhar-dry-port-arrests-kathmandu.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 414 for the project as a whole, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The project's environmental assessment states that all the dry port land is government-owned and that no further acquisition, resettlement or compensation was needed for it, a statement the requesters dispute.

chobhar-dry-port-arrests-kathmandu.confidence_note: The arrests are reported by The Kathmandu Post, which names its source, and separately by the people who filed the Request for Inspection; the two counts differ by two and both are given. The works stoppage and the withheld disbursements are recorded in the Bank's own documents. What is not established is the merit of the land claims: the Inspection Panel declined to investigate, so no finding exists either way, and the historical land dispute goes back to the 1960s, long before the Bank's involvement. The 416 unpaid cement factory workers and the uncompensated house demolitions are claims by the Chobhar Conservation Committee, denied in part by the implementing board, and are given here as claims.

tripoli-tyre-heritage-market-relocation.title: Households and market vendors moved for heritage works in Tripoli, Tyre and Saida
tripoli-tyre-heritage-market-relocation.place: Khan el Askar and the old souks, Tripoli, with the covered markets of Tyre and Saida, Lebanon
tripoli-tyre-heritage-market-relocation.point: Khan el Askar, the quarter in Tripoli's old city whose residents were physically relocated under two resettlement action plans. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search for Khan el Askar, Tripoli.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Additional Financing for the Cultural Heritage and Urban Development Project, project number P116197, loan IBRD-81370, US$27.0 million, approved 12 April 2012, with effectiveness delayed by a hung parliament. It topped up the original project, number P050529, loan IBRD-71660, US$31.5 million, approved 17 April 2003. One completion report covers both, dated 15 June 2017, and the operation closed on 31 December 2016. The additional loan paid for the later batches of the same works in the same five cities: US$17.9 million of it for rehabilitation of historic city centres and urban infrastructure, US$6.7 million for archaeological sites, US$2.2 million for institutional strengthening. The completion report rates the outcome Satisfactory and safeguards Satisfactory; the Independent Evaluation Group rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, assessing efficiency as modest because of high cost overruns (ICR Review, 22 November 2017). The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group also published a field-based Project Performance Assessment Report on 13 August 2019.

companies.name: Council for Development and Reconstruction of the Republic of Lebanon
companies.role: Implementing agency named in the completion report. A public body reporting to the Lebanese Council of Ministers that contracts and supervises state infrastructure works; two staff of the Directorate General of Antiquities worked full time on its premises to handle archaeological finds. No construction contractor is named in the documents.

tripoli-tyre-heritage-market-relocation.community: The works involved involuntary resettlement affecting 760 project-affected people across Tripoli, Tyre and Saida. Six resettlement action plans were prepared. The completion report's own table records what happened: 38 households with 209 people physically relocated from Khan el Askar blocks A and B in Tripoli; 33 households with 124 people physically relocated from Khan el Askar block C; 280 vendors physically relocated into the new marketplace in Tripoli; 3 tenants temporarily relocated from the Salameh building in Saida; and 144 vendors temporarily relocated for the new marketplace in Tyre. A sixth plan, for the physical relocation of 31 people from small shops and warehouses at Khan el-Askar, was never implemented because that component was cancelled. The Tripoli marketplace works were halted for four years from 2012 by active shooting in the city, the census of affected people had to be redone, and that plan was finished three months after the project closed. The Bank's field assessment, published in 2019, found that in the rebuilt covered market in Tyre the expected gains had not arrived: on the day of the visit the market was deserted and the vegetable and fruit sellers were playing cards for want of customers. Interviews recorded fewer permanent vendors working in the market than the resettlement plan had arranged for, fruit and vegetable sellers undercut by traders outside the market who pay no fees, and parking cut to 36 spaces where vendors had been told there would be 180. The market association collected the signatures of hundreds of vendors opposed to the changes and organised two sit-ins. In Tripoli, residents of the historic souk houses told the assessment team they had not been contacted before or during the works and had gone to the engineers on site themselves. Shop owners and tenants in the old souks said they were consulted and promised their objections would be considered, and felt that did not happen. Against this, the completion report says all six plans were financed by the project, four were satisfactorily implemented by closing, the Tripoli plan was satisfactorily implemented by the time of the report, and the new Tripoli marketplace won the Bank's 2017 Sustainable Development Vice-Presidency award.
tripoli-tyre-heritage-market-relocation.outcome: The operation closed on 31 December 2016 and the Tripoli marketplace resettlement finished three months later. The Bank's own field assessment of 2019 found the Tyre market underused and traditional businesses around the new public square losing trade, with owners saying the area was being turned over to tourism.
tripoli-tyre-heritage-market-relocation.displaced_label: households, physically relocated from Khan el Askar in Tripoli: the sum of the two rows of the completion report's Table 8 that record physical relocation of residents, 38 households with 209 people from blocks A and B and 33 households with 124 people from block C (completion report of 15 June 2017). Separately the same table records 280 vendors physically relocated into the new Tripoli marketplace, and temporary relocation of 3 tenants in Saida and 144 vendors in Tyre.
tripoli-tyre-heritage-market-relocation.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 371 for the additional financing, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The completion report's own total of people affected is 760 across the whole operation.

sources.title: Lebanon - Cultural Heritage and Urban Development Project and Additional Financing: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P050529, P116197)
Lebanon - Cultural Heritage and Urban Development Project: Implementation Completion Report (ICR) Review, Independent Evaluation Group
Lebanon - Cultural Heritage and Urban Development Project: Project Performance Assessment Report, Independent Evaluation Group

tripoli-tyre-heritage-market-relocation.confidence_note: All three documents are the lender's own, although the Project Performance Assessment Report rests on the Evaluation Group's own field visits and interviews in Tyre, Baalbek and Tripoli rather than on the project's reporting, and it contradicts the completion report's account of the Tyre market. No independent Lebanese press report, court record or audit on these relocations was found. The 71 households in the displaced field is the sum of two rows of one table in the completion report, both in the same unit and both carrying the phrase physical relocation of residents; no single document states 71.

nagapattinam-canal-demolition-tsunami-re.title: Homes demolished without compensation on the North Buckingham canal in Nagapattinam
nagapattinam-canal-demolition-tsunami-re.place: Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu, India, with resettlement sites at Okkiyum-Thuraipakkam and north Chennai
nagapattinam-canal-demolition-tsunami-re.point: Nagapattinam, the district headquarters of the district where the completion report places the demolitions. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search for Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu. The exact stretch of the North Buckingham canal is not named in the documents.

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Emergency Tsunami Reconstruction Project, project number P094513, credit IDA-40540, approved 3 May 2005 after the December 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, effective 9 August 2005, closing extended from 30 April 2008 to 31 December 2011. US$235.0 million of the credit was cancelled because the closing date was not extended further. The completion report of 18 June 2012 rates the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Unsatisfactory and borrower performance Moderately Unsatisfactory; the Independent Evaluation Group rates the outcome Unsatisfactory against the revised objective (ICR Review, 29 May 2013).

companies.name: Commissioner of Revenue Administration, Revenue Administration, Disaster Management and Mitigation Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
companies.role: Lead implementing agency named in the completion report, the state department that runs disaster relief and holds the district collectors under it. Thirteen implementing agencies carried out procurement; the Tamil Nadu Slum Clearance Board held the urban housing and the transit accommodation. No construction contractor is named for the canal works.

nagapattinam-canal-demolition-tsunami-re.community: The completion report records that in Nagapattinam district, work to improve the North Buckingham canal ran ahead of the state's resettlement and rehabilitation policy: the local authorities demolished the affected structures without offering compensation and assistance. After the Bank's team learned of it, the Government of Tamil Nadu drew up retrofit measures and put them in place, and all six displaced families were offered cash grants for the impacts they had suffered. Five families had received the grant when the credit closed on 31 December 2011 and the state was still in the process of paying the sixth. At two resettlement sites built for tsunami-affected people, about 100 families of the existing host population were affected: at Okkiyum-Thuraipakkam all 29 host families were moved temporarily into nearby Slum Clearance Board housing to wait for permanent houses, and at the All India Radio site in north Chennai 60 of 70 families had shifted by the closing date, leaving 10 families in temporary shelter awaiting a permanent site. For the resettlement sites as a whole, 560 hectares of land was acquired, 330 hectares of it private land, bought by private negotiation under a special government order letting district collectors set compensation at up to 200 per cent of guideline or registered values; about 40 hectares was donated by local citizens. The completion report says state funds, not Bank funds, paid for that land. The Independent Evaluation Group records that the project team told it the project was in compliance with the resettlement policy at the time the completion report was written, and that the 100 families physically displaced in Tamil Nadu were either given alternative housing or were expected to be shortly; that is a statement by Bank staff, not a document.
nagapattinam-canal-demolition-tsunami-re.killed_note: The completion report gives tsunami death and injury figures for the disaster itself, not for the project: 5,792 people reported missing and 6,913 injured in one passage, and 3,504 injured with 472,000 dislocated in another. Those are the disaster's toll and nothing in the documents attributes any death to the works.
nagapattinam-canal-demolition-tsunami-re.outcome: The credit closed on 31 December 2011 without a further extension, with one of the six Nagapattinam families still waiting for its grant and 10 host families at the north Chennai site still in temporary shelter. The completion report lists the difficulty of decommissioning and demolishing transit shelters, and unwillingness among beneficiaries to accept temporary relocation, among the lessons of in-situ urban resettlement.
nagapattinam-canal-demolition-tsunami-re.displaced_label: families, displaced in Nagapattinam district by improvement of the North Buckingham canal, whose structures the local authorities demolished without offering compensation or assistance (completion report of 18 June 2012, paragraph 53). Separately 29 host families were resettled temporarily at Okkiyum-Thuraipakkam and 60 of 70 host families had shifted at the north Chennai site by the closing date.
nagapattinam-canal-demolition-tsunami-re.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 360 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved.

sources.title: India - Emergency Tsunami Reconstruction Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P094513)
India - Emergency Tsunami Reconstruction Project: Implementation Completion Report (ICR) Review, Independent Evaluation Group

nagapattinam-canal-demolition-tsunami-re.confidence_note: The demolition without compensation is stated plainly in the Bank's completion report and repeated in the Independent Evaluation Group's review, but both are the lender's own documents and neither names the stretch of canal or the village. No Indian press report, court record or audit of this demolition was found. The completion report does not say which component financed the North Buckingham canal works; it records the demolition in the project's own social safeguards section. The report also does not say whether the sixth family was ever paid.

dhaka-khal-rehabilitation-eviction.title: An uncounted eviction on a Dhaka drainage canal, and seven canals dropped over resettlement
dhaka-khal-rehabilitation-eviction.place: Khilgaon-Bashabo canal and other drainage canals, Dhaka, Bangladesh
dhaka-khal-rehabilitation-eviction.point: Khilgaon, Dhaka, through which runs the Khilgaon-Bashabo canal, the one canal the completion report names in connection with a demolition. The canal where the eviction took place is not named. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search for Khilgaon, Dhaka.

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Dhaka Water Supply and Sanitation Project, project number P093988, credit IDA-45060, approved 2 December 2008, effective 17 March 2009, closing extended from 30 June 2013 to 30 June 2016. Almost half the credit was cancelled at the June 2013 restructuring. The completion report of 21 December 2016 rates the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Unsatisfactory, borrower performance Moderately Unsatisfactory and risk to development outcome Substantial; the Independent Evaluation Group also rates the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory (ICR Review, 8 March 2017).

companies.name: Dhaka Water Supply and Sewerage Authority
companies.role: Implementing agency named in the completion report. The statutory utility for water, sewerage and storm drainage in Dhaka; its Project Management Unit ran the works and was understaffed, and the project paid to build its resettlement capacity and to set up a low-income customer team inside it.

dhaka-khal-rehabilitation-eviction.community: The project re-excavated and improved drainage canals, known as khals, and built storm water pumping stations at Rampura and Kamlapur. No private land was acquired. The completion report records that the two pumping stations affected 221 households and the canal works affected 216 households, and says these were adequately compensated under the resettlement plans. A footnote to the report records something the main text does not: on one of the canals an eviction took place, of an unknown number of people. The utility rushed a tracer study to find them, but because the study risked being incomplete that canal was dropped from the project, and seven canals in all were dropped over complex resettlement issues. A complaint was received about the partial demolition of a building in the right of way of the Khilgaon-Bashabo canal; the report says that issue was adequately resolved. The report also records land subsidence at the Kamlapur pumping station site with no injuries, and one compensation payment for trees felled on a work site. The report states there are no outstanding environmental or social safeguards issues in the project.
dhaka-khal-rehabilitation-eviction.outcome: The project closed on 30 June 2016. Seven canals had been dropped rather than resettled, one of them after an eviction the project could not account for. No document was found giving the number of people evicted or what became of them.
dhaka-khal-rehabilitation-eviction.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 310 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The completion report gives no count of people relocated and says the number evicted on one canal is unknown.

sources.title: Bangladesh - Dhaka Water Supply and Sanitation Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P093988)
Bangladesh - Dhaka Water Supply and Sanitation Project: Implementation Completion Report (ICR) Review, Independent Evaluation Group

dhaka-khal-rehabilitation-eviction.confidence_note: The eviction rests on a single footnote of the Bank's own completion report, with no count of people, no canal named and no date. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of that report does not mention it. The report's own main text says there are no outstanding social safeguards issues and that affected households were adequately compensated. The two counts of households affected by canal works do not agree between parts of the same report: the main text and the annex give 216 households compensated along the canals, while the borrower's section says the improvements on nine canals affected 187 persons or households, 67 of them encroachers the framework made ineligible for resettlement assistance. The report's results table gives 441 project-affected households successfully compensated against a target of 500. No independent Bangladeshi press report, court record or audit on these canal evictions was found.

thimphu-land-pooling-compensation-arrear.title: Structures and businesses lost to land pooling in Thimphu, with three owners never traced or paid
thimphu-land-pooling-compensation-arrear.place: Dechencholing, Lanjopakha and Taba local area plans, Thimphu, Bhutan
thimphu-land-pooling-compensation-arrear.point: Dechencholing, Thimphu, the first of the three local area plans whose land pooling plans were implemented and handed to the city in September 2013. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search for Dechencholing, Thimphu.

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Second Bhutan Urban Development Project, project number P090157, credit IDA-47440 of US$12.0 million approved 29 April 2010, with additional credit IDA-54310 of US$17.4 million; effective 24 August 2010, closing extended from 31 December 2015 to 30 June 2019; US$24.8 million disbursed of US$29.4 million. The completion report of 27 December 2019 rates social safeguard compliance Satisfactory (paragraph 67); the Independent Evaluation Group reviewed it on 16 March 2020.

companies.name: Thimphu Thromde
companies.role: Implementing agency named in the completion report, alongside the Ministry of Works and Human Settlements. Thimphu's municipal corporation; its Urban Planning Division ran the social impact work and its Social Development and Resettlement Cell, which the completion report says the city could not fully staff, handled resettlement. The unpaid compensation sits in the Thromde's accounts section. No construction contractor is named in the documents.

thimphu-land-pooling-compensation-arrear.community: The project serviced three new neighbourhoods in Thimphu by land pooling: landowners kept their plots but gave up a share of their land for roads and services instead of the state buying it outright. The Independent Evaluation Group records that title owners who agreed to the approach contributed 25 per cent of their land and were to receive compensation for structures, other assets and livelihood, plus resettlement assistance. The completion report lists what people lost: physical structures, fruit trees, businesses and access to rental houses because of the land pooling, and temporary restrictions on agricultural land where water mains were laid. Neither document counts the structures or the households. A footnote to the completion report records that when the project ended only three affected households or persons were left to be paid, because they could not be tracked despite repeated efforts, and that their compensation has been kept in the Thromde's accounts section and is available for payment. A grievance committee met regularly on complaints about land pooling and compensation payments, and verified payments before they went up for approval. A beneficiary survey found that 60 per cent of residents in Dechencholing, 60 per cent in Lanjopakha and 54 per cent in Taba reported better quality of life since moving to the new neighbourhood.
thimphu-land-pooling-compensation-arrear.outcome: The project closed on 30 June 2019. Three affected owners had still not been found or paid, and their money remained with Thimphu Thromde. The completion report presents the land pooling itself as a success, saying it cut the government's land acquisition and compensation costs and is now being asked for in other areas, such as the settlement of Kabesa next to Dechencholing.
thimphu-land-pooling-compensation-arrear.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 279 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. Neither the completion report nor its review counts people relocated, or structures lost.

sources.title: Bhutan - Second Bhutan Urban Development Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P090157)
Bhutan - BT: Urban Development II: Implementation Completion Report (ICR) Review, Independent Evaluation Group

thimphu-land-pooling-compensation-arrear.confidence_note: This is a thin case and rests entirely on the lender's own documents. The harm is a list of kinds of loss with no count attached, plus three named-as-three owners never traced or paid, recorded in a footnote. The completion report rates social safeguard compliance Satisfactory and the Independent Evaluation Group's review repeats that compensation payments were made to the affected people. No Bhutanese press report, court record or audit on the Thimphu land pooling compensation was found.

iraq-expressway-worker-deaths-vendor-rel.title: Three worker deaths and the moving of 72 roadside shops on Iraq's Expressway 1
iraq-expressway-worker-deaths-vendor-rel.place: Expressway No. 1 between Nasiriya and Basra, Iraq, with the Girsheen-Suheila section of the North-South corridor in Dohuk governorate
iraq-expressway-worker-deaths-vendor-rel.point: Nasiriya, the northern end of segment R7 of Expressway No. 1, the stretch where the roadside shops stood and where the project was partly suspended over resettlement. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search for Nasiriyah, Iraq.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Transport Corridors Project, project number P131550, loan IBRD-83220, US$355.0 million, approved 19 December 2013, loan agreement signed 2 March 2014, effective 30 March 2015 after a twelve-month delay while a government was formed, closing extended from 31 December 2019 to 30 June 2023, US$337.6 million disbursed. The project was assigned environmental category A and triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment and involuntary resettlement. Part of the loan was suspended for disbursement over failure to comply fully with the social safeguards policy, specifically over updating and implementing the resettlement plan for the vendors along segments R7 and R8 (completion report of 18 December 2023, paragraph 73). The completion report rates the outcome Highly Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory and quality of monitoring Modest; the Independent Evaluation Group rates the outcome Satisfactory and quality of monitoring Substantial (ICR Review, 2 May 2024, section 11).

companies.name: State Commission for Roads and Bridges, Ministry of Construction, Housing, Municipalities and Public Works, Iraq
companies.role: Implementing agency named in the completion report, which ran the works through project management teams at the Commission and at the Roads and Bridges Directorate. The completion report says the larger works contracts were awarded to international contractors but names none of them.

iraq-expressway-worker-deaths-vendor-rel.community: Three workers were killed on the project. The completion report gives the cause of each: the driver of a pick-up van who collided with a parked vehicle; a supervising engineer run over by a project vehicle during site supervision; and a daily worker hit by a pick-up car while standing on the road. The report says these incidents were completely avoidable had higher levels of worker awareness, training, safety provisions and close supervision been in place. Several traffic accidents happened during the rehabilitation of long sections of Expressway No. 1, both inside and outside the temporary traffic management zones; the report records no deaths among the public inside those zones, and says the Bank required the project team to report and document accidents at once, a practice that did not exist before, under threat of suspending disbursement. On segments R7 and R8, 72 shop owners immediately next to the right of way were resettled to dedicated serviced lay-bys, and those who had been trading informally were legalised. The completion report presents this as a gain: compensating squatters rather than only landlords was new in Iraq, the poorest traders benefited, and vendors were able to expand their premises at the new location, with better access and parking. The project was partly suspended for disbursement because the resettlement plan for these vendors was not updated and implemented to the Bank's satisfaction. On the new Girsheen-Suheila road corridor in the north, land had to be acquired, and the plan covered the amount of farmland taken, crop loss, who was eligible, the rates for crops and fixed assets, and extra help for three affected people below the poverty line. Delays in paying affected people were observed and the Bank reminded the roads directorate that no civil work could start on the ground before the compensation was paid. All compensation due was disbursed by May 2016.
iraq-expressway-worker-deaths-vendor-rel.killed_note: The completion report separately records the improper reporting to the Bank of two accidental deaths, of the resident engineer and of the contractor, between July 2017 and August 2018 on the same two segments. The documents do not say whether these two are among the three worker fatalities listed with causes, so they are not added here.
iraq-expressway-worker-deaths-vendor-rel.outcome: The project closed on 30 June 2023. The completion report rates its outcome Highly Satisfactory and the Independent Evaluation Group rates it Satisfactory. Average traffic deaths across the project road segments for 2020 to 2023 came to 23 a year against a baseline of 113 and a target of 87. The report says the project obliged contractors to comply with occupational health and safety procedures and to provide workers with sanitary dormitories and paid rest time.
iraq-expressway-worker-deaths-vendor-rel.displaced_label: shop owners, resettled from immediately beside the right of way of Expressway No. 1 segments R7 and R8 to dedicated serviced lay-bys (completion report of 18 December 2023, paragraph 72, and ICR Review of 2 May 2024).
iraq-expressway-worker-deaths-vendor-rel.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 256 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved.

sources.title: Iraq - Transport Corridors Project: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P131550)
Iraq - IQ-Transport Corridors Project: Implementation Completion Report (ICR) Review, Independent Evaluation Group
Loan Agreement, Loan Number 8322-IQ, Transport Corridors Project, conformed

iraq-expressway-worker-deaths-vendor-rel.confidence_note: The deaths, the resettlement of the shop owners and the partial suspension of disbursement all come from the Bank's own completion report, with the Independent Evaluation Group's review repeating them, so the lender is reporting on its own project. No Iraqi press report, court record or audit on the worker deaths was found. The cause given for each of the three deaths is a vehicle collision, and the report's judgement that they were avoidable is its own. Whether the two accidental deaths of July 2017 to August 2018 are separate from the three is not resolved by either document.

jordan-heritage-cities-house-shop-demoli.title: Houses and shops demolished for heritage and tourism works in five Jordanian towns
jordan-heritage-cities-house-shop-demoli.place: Jerash, Karak, Salt, Ajloun and Madaba, Jordan
jordan-heritage-cities-house-shop-demoli.point: Jerash, the town with the largest commercial demolition and the largest resettlement cost of the five. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search for Jerash, Jordan.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Third Tourism Development Project, Cultural Heritage, Tourism and Urban Development, project number P081823, loan IBRD-74260, US$56.0 million at approval on 30 January 2007, reduced to US$55.0 million, effective 16 August 2007, closing extended from 30 September 2012 to 31 March 2014, US$50.78 million disbursed. Land acquisition, expropriation and resettlement cost US$7.60 million against US$5.86 million estimated at appraisal, and a Level 1 restructuring of 14 July 2011 raised the allocation to cover it. The completion report of 30 January 2015 rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory and risk to development outcome Substantial; the Independent Evaluation Group also rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory and rates risk to development outcome Significant (ICR Review, 9 June 2015).

companies.name: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Jordan
companies.role: Implementing agency named in the completion report. Its Technical Development Department ran the project unit; the appraisal document planned to recruit 17 extra staff for it. The completion report rates the department's performance Moderately Satisfactory, mainly on poor monitoring. No construction contractor is named in the documents.

jordan-heritage-cities-house-shop-demoli.community: The works ran through densely built town centres and took land and buildings. The completion report's own table gives what was actually done against what was planned. Permanent land acquisition came to 12,408 square metres against 20,332 planned. Residential houses were demolished over 2,905 square metres against 4,107 planned, 2,505 of it in Karak and 400 in Jerash. Commercial stores were demolished over 1,750 square metres against 7,136 planned, 1,555 of it in Jerash and 195 in Ajloun. Forty-six households were affected against 52 planned: 6 in Jerash, 11 in Karak, 17 in Salt and 12 in Ajloun. Madaba had none. In Ajloun, vendors had to be relocated before the works could start, and the report says that and land acquisition in Salt were where the process took longest. The actual resettlement cost was higher than planned, 4.96 million Jordanian dinars against 4.18 million, about US$7 million against US$5.9 million, because the compensation actually paid was higher than planned. The completion report says compensation rates for all lost assets were set on market value and reflected replacement cost, that community liaison officers in each city acted between the municipalities and affected people, that all affected people were satisfied with the compensation and resettlement package, and that renters eventually returned to improved and renovated shops.
jordan-heritage-cities-house-shop-demoli.outcome: The project closed on 31 March 2014. The documents record no outstanding compensation and no unresolved grievance. The Independent Evaluation Group notes that the main text of the completion report does not discuss compliance with the policy on cultural property, and that the borrower's own comments record a few minor issues found during construction and corrected.
jordan-heritage-cities-house-shop-demoli.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 231 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The completion report counts households affected, square metres of land taken and square metres of housing and shops demolished, and gives no count of people relocated.
jordan-heritage-cities-house-shop-demoli.displaced_label: No count of people relocated appears in the completion report; 46 households were affected and 2,905 square metres of residential housing and 1,750 square metres of commercial stores were demolished.

sources.title: Jordan - Third Tourism Development Project: Cultural Heritage, Tourism and Urban Development: Implementation Completion and Results Report (P081823)
Jordan - Cultural Heritage, Tourism and Urban Development: Implementation Completion Report (ICR) Review, Independent Evaluation Group

jordan-heritage-cities-house-shop-demoli.confidence_note: The demolition figures are actual outcome figures in a table that prints the plan beside them, so they are not a plan reprinted as a result, and the Independent Evaluation Group's review quotes the same numbers. But both documents are the lender's own, and both record that compensation was paid at replacement cost, that affected people were satisfied, and that renters went back to renovated shops. What this case rests on is that homes and shops were demolished and land was taken, not on anything going unpaid. No Jordanian press report, court record or audit on these expropriations was found.

kabeli-transmission-line-compensation-ar.title: Nearly half the compensation unpaid on the Kabeli corridor transmission line
kabeli-transmission-line-compensation-ar.place: Kabeli corridor 132 kV transmission line, Jhapa, Ilam and Panchthar districts, eastern Nepal
kabeli-transmission-line-compensation-ar.point: Phidim, Panchthar district, on the line's second and third sections and the town where the route had to be changed after local protest. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search for Phidim, Nepal.

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Kabeli Transmission Project, project number P112893, credit IDA-49320 and grant IDA-H6760, approved 10 May 2011, effective 21 September 2011, closing extended by 18 months from 30 June 2015 to 31 December 2016. Component 1 paid for a 90 km 132 kV double circuit transmission line and four substations. The completion report of 12 September 2018 rates the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Unsatisfactory, borrower performance Moderately Unsatisfactory and risk to development outcome High; the Independent Evaluation Group concurs on the outcome, rating it Moderately Unsatisfactory (ICR Review, 14 January 2019). The Evaluation Group's review says social safeguards were only partially implemented and that 55 per cent of compensation for project-affected families was paid.

companies.name: Nepal Electricity Authority
companies.role: Implementing agency named in the completion report. The state-owned utility that generates, transmits and distributes electricity in Nepal; it acquired the land and pays the compensation, and the report says preparation of its resettlement action plan was delayed and the issue was raised repeatedly with its management. Its Deputy Managing Director was handling the two unpaid categories. The Alternative Energy Promotion Centre implemented the rural energy component. No construction contractor is named in the documents.

kabeli-transmission-line-compensation-ar.community: The line runs for 90 km through hill districts of eastern Nepal and needed tower pads, a right of way and the removal of structures. Eighteen months after the project closed, the completion report of September 2018 printed the state of the payments. For tower pads, 188 of 228 affected families had been paid, 82 per cent; the gaps are owners with no legal title, families unable to produce legal documents, and families unwilling to accept the compensation. For structures, 41 of 82 families had been paid, 50 per cent; three families received only half because they had not yet demolished their structures, one was not paid because the landowner was absent, and 37 structures had only recently been identified and were still being valued. For the right-of-way easement fee, 673 of 1,339 affected families had been paid, 50 per cent; the gaps are difficulty identifying owners and users because the district land survey offices have no record, payments left uncollected because the amount is too small to bother with, and absentees. Resettlement and rehabilitation assistance to the owners of residential structures had still not been paid, which the report attributes to a change in senior management, and assistance to people without title had not been paid because the chief district officer was unwilling to carry out the valuation. A community school in the right of way was being rebuilt, with completion expected by the end of December 2018. Land acquisition was still going on at the closing date for the sections still under construction, and the report says the acquisition was held back mainly by delay in agreeing the compensation amount. Dissatisfaction persisted among the communities and households whose land was affected, and persistent local protest forced the line to be re-routed around about 3.8 km of the peri-urban edge of Jorsal in Phidim right at the end of the project; the report says there is no community resistance there now. The report adds that the Bank has found the utility's safeguard performance satisfactory and that the utility has committed in writing to finish the measures during construction.
kabeli-transmission-line-compensation-ar.outcome: Only the 34.5 km first section, Damak to Godak, was physically complete when the project closed on 31 December 2016; the substations stood finished but uncommissioned for a long time because no line was there to carry power to them. An external monitor was hired to follow the resettlement plan. As of August 2018, 55 per cent of the compensation due to project-affected families had been paid. The line's third section was put into service in August 2019.
kabeli-transmission-line-compensation-ar.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 203 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The completion report counts project-affected families paid and unpaid, and gives no count of people relocated.

Nepal - Kabeli Transmission Project: Implementation Completion Report (ICR) Review, Independent Evaluation Group
Locals demand revision of power line alignment, The Kathmandu Post
Protest halts Kabeli Corridor project in Ilam, The Himalayan Times
Land compensation and right-of-way issues delay power line projects, The Kathmandu Post

kabeli-transmission-line-compensation-ar.confidence_note: The payment figures come from the Bank's completion report, sourced in the report to the project itself in August 2018, and are repeated by the Independent Evaluation Group, so the count of unpaid families rests on the lender's own reporting. Nepali press corroborates the surrounding dispute but not the figures: The Kathmandu Post reported in April 2016 that a committee formed by 67 houses in wards 4, 5, 7 and 9 of Phidim municipality opposed the alignment, and The Himalayan Times reported in July 2017 that work had stood still for two months at Siddithumka in Ilam and at Panchami bazaar in Deumai after locals objected that towers were being put up against the environmental assessment and demanded they be moved away from markets and settlements or that people be compensated. The Kathmandu Post reported in October 2019 that the Kabeli project was among several held up by disagreements over land compensation and right of way, without giving figures.

india-power-system-development-iii-wardh.drop_reason: Neither limb of the forward rule is met. The completion report of 30 January 2012 says of the whole project that POWERGRID ensures that its projects do not result in physical displacement of the local population, and that under this project social assessment and a rehabilitation action plan were done for the Wardha substation only. Its Annex 3 scheme table records the outcome for Wardha: the plan involved 89.20 acres of Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation land, no land compensation was required to be paid to any project affected families as the land belonged to that corporation, and the plan was completed in March 2008 with rehabilitation assistance of INR 3.62 lakh distributed to all affected families and vocational training given to them at Krishi Kendra, Wardha. The three adverse findings checked all resolve: the report records that implementation of the plan was delayed by the long process of acquiring land and extending resettlement entitlements through the district administration, and that implementation of the community development part was unduly delayed by staffing constraints, which together with forest clearance delays got overall safeguard compliance downgraded to moderately satisfactory towards the end of 2008; the same paragraph records that an independent external agency's impact assessment found an improvement in the socioeconomic status of a majority of the affected people, and the rating was upgraded to satisfactory in early 2011. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 12 November 2012 gives the same account and adds nothing adverse. The only people-bearing figures in the project's resettlement papers are counts of people affected, not relocated, and they belong to another substation: the resettlement plan of 1 March 2007 covers the 400/220 kV Solapur substation at Limbi-Chincholi, giving 19 of 487 village households affected by the substation, 35 affected families and 129 people affected out of 2,278, and it is a plan for a scheme under Western Region System Strengthening II, not one of the four substations the completion report lists under this project. What is left is a count of people affected, which is a drop under the forward rule.

egypt-wind-power-transmission-line-samal.drop_reason: Neither limb of the forward rule is met. The completion report of 30 May 2020 records at paragraph 58 that the transmission lines and substations were built almost entirely in desert where the land belongs to the government and is mostly uninhabited; that a resettlement action plan was prepared only for the overhead line from the Gulf of Suez substation to the Samallout substation, because that line took land for tower footings and damaged crops temporarily around the inhabited areas at the Nile crossing; that the tower-footing land was acquired on a willing seller-willing buyer basis and crop damage was compensated at prevailing assessed market rates; that no significant disputes were recorded by the grievance mechanism, the cases received being mainly requests to explain how the compensation rates were worked out; and that no resettlement plans were prepared for the substations because all were on government-owned uninhabited desert land. The appraisal document of 19 May 2010 says no land acquisition is associated with almost 89 per cent of the route. The resettlement action plan of 1 February 2014 is a plan and gives 22 owners in its census; no outcome document carries that figure or any count of people moved. The occupational health and safety finding was checked: both the completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of 4 February 2021 record instances of non-compliance with occupational health and safety requirements and unsatisfactory on-site contractor performance, with the implementing utility hiring an independent consultancy late to monitor contractors, and both record that the efforts led to gradual improvement, insurance coverage for all workers and a workers' code of conduct. Neither document records a death, an injury, an arrest, land taken without payment or a livelihood not restored.

sri-lanka-provincial-roads-land-donation.drop_reason: Neither limb of the forward rule is met. The completion report of 28 December 2015 says at paragraph 36 that although no land acquisition was envisaged at the inception of the project the involuntary resettlement policy was triggered to cover possible adverse impacts, and that overall implementation of social safeguards was rated satisfactory throughout the project period. The borrower's section lists the data gathered for the resettlement plan under the heading land required through voluntary donation. On outcomes, paragraph 38 says the great majority of the works were road widening, culverts and drainage, and that most adverse impacts observed during implementation were construction related: access to houses and shops, damage to houses and boundary walls, and damage to side drains and toilet structures. It attaches no count to any of these and records that grievance redress mechanisms were set up in all participating provinces with a robust review and monitoring system. The borrower's section says all project affected people identified were provided mitigation measures for their livelihoods. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 10 June 2016 adds nothing adverse on resettlement and repeats that implementation of social safeguards was deemed satisfactory throughout. No document counts anyone relocated, records compensation unpaid or below replacement cost, or records a death, injury, arrest or livelihood not restored.

kiribati-bonriki-airport-land-claim.drop_reason: Neither limb of the forward rule is met. The completion report of 19 December 2019 says at paragraph 58 that the project's environmental and social safeguards management was satisfactory, and lists the safeguards issues that arose: compensation for trees that were cut down, a dwelling that was obstructing the obstacle limitation survey, asbestos to be removed and disposed of at Bonriki, and a land claim associated with the Bonriki terminal. It then says all of these were resolved at the completion of the project, and gives no count, no outcome and no date for the dwelling. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 6 May 2020 repeats the same list and says all were successfully resolved by project completion. The land claim was checked in the project's own social safeguards report of 5 December 2013, which records an ongoing dispute between the government and owners over a strip of land underlying the airport terminal and car park, that the dispute went through the courts to the High Court and is now resolved, and in a footnote that the government has the option of compulsory acquisition but that the outcome to date is that the government will be paying the lease including arrears to landowners. That land was already under the terminal before the project. No document counts anyone relocated or records compensation unpaid at close, a death, an injury, an arrest or a livelihood not restored.

karnataka-urban-water-land-acquisition.drop_reason: The outcome is land area plus a count of people affected, which round 22 settled is not limb (b). The completion report for this project is not in the harvest and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of 12 September 2012 is the only route to it; the review cites it by paragraph. At its safeguards section the review reports, citing the completion report, that the government prepared a land acquisition and resettlement policy framework satisfactory to the Bank and that resettlement action plans were prepared for Hubli-Dharwar and Gulbarga; that the Gulbarga plan was later modified because the pipelines were re-directed onto unencumbered government land, which reduced the number of affected families; that the total land acquisition for the project involved 8.41 hectares affecting 215 families, primarily in the Hubli-Dharwar and Gulbarga areas; and, citing completion report paragraph 2.4.5, that the plans were satisfactorily implemented and there were no complaints. The review reports environmental and safeguard management rated satisfactory over the entire project, and records that the project team subsequently informed the Evaluation Group that the project complied with the environmental assessment policy, which is a staff statement and not a document. ICIJ's estimate for this project, 215, is to the person the review's count of families affected. No document counts anyone relocated or records compensation unpaid or below replacement cost, a death, an injury, an arrest or a livelihood not restored.

southern-west-bank-landfill-waste-picker.drop_reason: Neither limb of the forward rule is met. The completion report for this project is not in the harvest and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of 22 May 2017 is the only route to it; the review cites it by page. The review reports full compliance with both the environmental assessment and involuntary resettlement policies, with safeguards instruments developed and disclosed before approval and a technical operations unit reporting quarterly on them. On the people whose living the project changed, it reports, citing the completion report, that all former waste pickers at the Yatta open dumpsite were given jobs, helped to find new jobs at the Joint Services Council, or trained to become economically independent, that under-age pickers were allowed into vocational schools, and that environmental and living conditions improved around the previous open dumpsites, which used to suffer from waste burning. The results indicator for compensation, settlements, employment and income-generating schemes for affected people, waste pickers and herders records 100 per cent of households against a target of 80 per cent. Land for the new landfill was paid for by a US$2.0 million borrower contribution. No document counts anyone relocated or records compensation unpaid or below replacement cost, a death, an injury, an arrest or a livelihood not restored. One figure in the review, that the project closed 19 uncontrolled dumpsites against a target of 17, is an output and not a harm.
